submission_commit_message.stdout:
riscv: Fix load_unaligned_zeropad() on RV32

load_unaligned_zeropad() issues REG_L, which is lw on RV32 and ld on
RV64. Its exception handler nevertheless aligns every faulting address
to an eight-byte boundary and derives a shift from three address bits.

For an RV32 load starting in the last three bytes of a mapped page, this
selects an earlier four-byte word and shifts it by 40, 48, or 56 bits.
The destination register therefore does not contain the bytes at the
requested address followed by zero padding.

Derive the alignment and offset from the width of the data word. This
leaves RV64 behavior unchanged and makes RV32 use the correct source word
and a shift of 8, 16, or 24 bits.

Fixes: d0fdc20b0429 ("riscv: select DCACHE_WORD_ACCESS for efficient unaligned access HW")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Karl Mehltretter <kmehltretter@gmail.com>
